standard.notes: Firefighter II builds on FF I with expanded fireground coordination, more complex fire control, rescue support, and limited company-level responsibilities. States may add local modules.

title: Firefighter II
description: Complete advanced entry-level structural firefighter pathway: expanded knowledge, higher-level JPRs, coordinated evolutions, and certification readiness beyond Firefighter I.
audience: Firefighter I certified members seeking FF II
Probationary firefighters completing advanced academy modules
Volunteers advancing toward full structural qualification

estimatedRange.typicalHours: 40–120+ additional instructional hours after FF I (varies by state/academy)
estimatedRange.typicalDuration: 1–6 weeks full-time module or extended part-time path

prerequisites.title: Firefighter I certification
prerequisites.detail: Current or recognized Firefighter I (state / IFSAC / Pro Board as required by the certifying entity).

prerequisites.title: HazMat Awareness / Operations currency
prerequisites.detail: Many systems expect current HazMat Awareness and Operations before or with FF II.

prerequisites.title: Program or department affiliation
prerequisites.detail: Some states require membership in an organized department or enrollment in an approved advanced program.

corequisitesAndCommonCompanions.title: Hazardous Materials Operations
corequisitesAndCommonCompanions.notes: Often treated as part of the complete structural package.

corequisitesAndCommonCompanions.title: ICS 200 (or equivalent)
corequisitesAndCommonCompanions.notes: Supports multi-unit coordination concepts introduced at FF II.

knowledgeDomains.title: Advanced fire behavior and building systems
topics: Fire dynamics in larger or more complex structures
Effects of ventilation and flow paths
Building systems and hazards (HVAC, elevators, utilities)

knowledgeDomains.title: Company operations and coordination
topics: Assignment of roles within a company

knowledgeDomains.title: Rescue support and specialized awareness
topics: Assisting technical rescue teams at the operations level as trained
Victim removal under more complex conditions

knowledgeDomains.title: Public assistance and non-fire emergencies
topics: Assisting the public during non-fire incidents
Basic electrical / gas / water emergency awareness
Scene safety for mixed hazard responses

jprSkillGroups.title: Coordinated fire attack and company evolution
jprSkillGroups.standardRef: NFPA 1001 – Firefighter II fire control related JPRs
skills: Operate as part of a coordinated interior attack team
Support exposure protection assignments
Advance and operate hoselines in more complex layouts
Communicate conditions and needs to company officer

jprSkillGroups.title: Foam application (where required by curriculum)
jprSkillGroups.standardRef: NFPA 1001 – foam related JPRs where adopted
skills: Prepare and apply foam for Class B scenarios as trained
Select appropriate foam equipment and concentrate handling practices

jprSkillGroups.title: Vehicle extrication support
skills: Stabilize a vehicle as trained
Assist with glass management and patient access
Operate common extrication tools under supervision
Maintain scene safety and tool discipline

jprSkillGroups.title: Assist specialized rescue operations
jprSkillGroups.standardRef: NFPA 1001 – assist technical rescue related JPRs
skills: Support rope, confined space, or trench awareness tasks only as trained and authorized
Establish exclusion zones and basic support functions
Recognize limits of FF II vs technician-level work

jprSkillGroups.title: Fire cause / origin support awareness
skills: Protect potential evidence during overhaul
Recognize and report obvious indicators without disturbing scene beyond assignment

jprSkillGroups.title: Public service and utility control support
jprSkillGroups.standardRef: NFPA 1001 – public assist / utility related JPRs
skills: Control utilities as trained and ordered
Assist civilians during non-fire emergencies
Illuminate and make safe common hazard scenes

jprSkillGroups.title: Expanded communications and reporting
skills: Deliver clear condition and progress reports
Operate within multi-unit radio plans
Support accountability systems

jprSkillGroups.title: Equipment and hose service testing awareness
jprSkillGroups.standardRef: NFPA 1001 – service testing / maintenance related JPRs where included
skills: Perform assigned equipment checks
Assist with hose service testing procedures as trained
Document deficiencies

trainingSequence.title: Verify Firefighter I and companion credentials
actions: Confirm FF I is current and accepted by the testing entity
Confirm HazMat and medical requirements are current
Enroll in approved FF II program or module

trainingSequence.title: Advanced theory block
actions: Company coordination and ICS support concepts
Rescue support and public assist theory

trainingSequence.title: Advanced practical skill blocks
actions: Utility control and public service tasks

trainingSequence.title: Integrated multi-company style drills
actions: Practice communications and accountability under load
Live-fire only where authorized and compliant

trainingSequence.title: Testing and certification
actions: Submit documentation and obtain FF II certificate / seals

assessment.practical: Pass/fail advanced skill stations and coordinated evolutions
assessment.written: Multiple-choice exam on FF II knowledge objectives
assessment.passingCriteria: Set by state certifying entity or accredited academy

stateOverlayGuidance.howToUse: Record only state differences: required hours, whether foam or extrication modules are mandatory, testing entity, and reciprocity.
alwaysVerifyWith: IFSAC or Pro Board accredited entity

sources.title: NFPA 1001 Firefighter II professional qualifications
sources.note: Do not paste copyrighted JPR text verbatim.

disclaimer: Structured training roadmap for personal professional development. Not a substitute for state, academy, or department requirements.
